clue.text: Talkative little bird (have a heart, Poe !)

definitions.text: Talkative little bird (have a heart, Poe !)

parts.words: Talkative little bird (have a heart, Poe !)
parts.note: a chatterer is the 'little bird' that tells secrets, and adding 'heart' gives the title of Edgar Allan Poe's famous short story

explanation.surface: Someone begs Edgar Allan Poe to be kind to a chattering little bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A little bird told me' is the idiom for an informer; Poe's story of a murderer's beating heart is The Tell-Tale Heart.
explanation.definitionFit: A gossip who blabs secrets is a telltale, the informant behind 'a little bird told me'.

clue.text: The bird who suggests ability in the doubles ?

indicators.note: the clue's phrase only suggests the bird by its sound when said out loud

parts.note: in a doubles match it takes two players, so the ability of the pair is 'two can'

explanation.surface: A bird is credited with a knack for tennis doubles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two can' (the pair is able) is heard as the name of the big-billed tropical bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A brightly billed tropical American species is this bird.

clue.text: They're first to change ideals

indicators.note: the letters of the word ideals are made to change their order

explanation.surface: Someone notes which people are always first to alter their principles.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition comes from the courtesy 'ladies first'.
explanation.definitionFit: By the old courtesy, women are let through doors ahead of men.

clue.text: Make dull Jack point to his reform

parts.note: a jack tar is a sailor, so Jack gives TAR
N is a compass point, north

indicators.note: the letters of his must reform into a new order

explanation.surface: A sailor is urged to point himself towards mending his ways, which sounds dreary.
explanation.definitionFit: To tarnish metal is to dim its shine.

clue.text: Upper class in much, but a boorish type

indicators.note: the upper-class letter goes in the middle of the word for much

parts.note: a lot means much
U is the old label for upper-class usage

explanation.surface: An upper-class person is mostly in evidence yet behaves like a boor.
explanation.definitionFit: A loutish man is an uncouth, ill-mannered oaf.

clue.text: Long notes from Rome

parts.note: the musical notes of double length share a name with brief letters issued by the Pope

explanation.surface: Lengthy letters arrive from the Vatican.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'notes' as musical notes worth two whole notes, and also as papal letters sent from Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: A papal brief and a double whole note in music both carry this name.

clue.text: One of many derelict vacancies in Hamelin

definitions.text: One of many derelict vacancies in Hamelin

parts.words: One of many derelict vacancies in Hamelin
parts.note: after the Pied Piper led the vermin out of Hamelin, all their burrows stood empty

explanation.surface: Hamelin is full of abandoned empty homes.
explanation.walkthrough: The Pied Piper of Hamelin piped away all the town's rodents, leaving their holes vacant.
explanation.definitionFit: Each burrow left by the departed rodents is an empty hole once lived in by a rodent.

clue.text: Sal is so flighty

definitions.meaning: smelling salts, so the salt 'Sal' has this quality

explanation.walkthrough: SAL VOLATILE, smelling salts, gives the first reading: 'Sal' is so.
explanation.definitionFit: Smelling salts are named sal volatile, and a flighty temper is changeable and erratic.

clue.text: Romantic return from a space-sweep ?

parts.note: what a broom gathers after sweeping outer space is cosmic dust, also a word for a romantic glow

explanation.surface: Something romantic is collected while cleaning the cosmos.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both a magical, romantic quality and the fine particles from celestial bodies.

clue.text: A nice fillet for Pug !

parts.note: a cut of tenderloin beef, and also an upward blow a pugilist (Pug) throws

explanation.surface: Someone offers a pet dog a tasty piece of steak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pug' is not the dog but a boxer (pugilist), whose punch from below shares the name of a beef cut.
explanation.definitionFit: The tenderloin of beef and a rising punch in boxing both go by this name.

clue.text: She's all set for stardom

parts.note: a girl's name that is Latin for 'star', so she is born for stardom

explanation.surface: A young actress is ready to become famous.
explanation.definitionFit: The woman's name comes from the Latin word for a star.

clue.text: Primitive warning to a male

parts.note: cave is the Latin call 'beware!' once used by schoolboys as a warning
a man is a male

explanation.surface: Someone shouts a warning to a man.
explanation.walkthrough: CAVE (two syllables) was British public-school slang for 'look out!'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Stone Age dweller is the image of a primitive human, used as a noun here.

clue.text: This acid, in its place, tickles the palate

indicators.note: the clue says the acid is in the words that follow, so the answer sits inside them

explanation.surface: A sour ingredient, used in the right place, pleases the taste buds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in its' points inside 'place, tickles the palate', where the acid is hidden across the comma in 'place, tickles'; the rest of the words only dress the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The acid of vinegar gives salad dressing its sharp taste, and is named for the Latin word for vinegar.

clue.text: Leapt up when card vote was called for

indicators.note: the letters of card vote are called for in another order

explanation.surface: Someone jumped up when a card vote was demanded at a union meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: To caper and frolic about is to leap up in play.

clue.text: Stroke-player causes a giggle ?

definitions.meaning: in cricket a snick is a faint edge off the bat, so one who plays such a stroke

explanation.walkthrough: SNICK is the cricket term for a thin edge off the bat.
explanation.definitionFit: A batter who edges the ball snicks it, and a half-suppressed laugh is a snigger.

clue.text: French girls follow singer for edible fungi

indicators.note: the French girls come after the singer in the answer

parts.note: a chanter is one who sings
elles is French for 'they' of women, so French girls

explanation.surface: A group of French girls trail after a vocalist.
explanation.definitionFit: These golden, funnel-shaped mushrooms are prized wild edible fungi.

clue.text: Forks out at the end of play

definitions.meaning: in cricket the stumps are drawn when play ends for the day

explanation.definitionFit: To pay up grudgingly is a British idiom, and 'stumps' mark close of play in cricket.

clue.text: A belief's possible to be put into practice

indicators.note: the letters of a belief's are worked over and practised into a new arrangement

parts.note: the possessive s is kept as a letter here

explanation.surface: A belief may be practicable if acted upon.
explanation.definitionFit: Something workable is achievable and so possible.

clue.text: Opportunity at choir school audition ? You bet !

definitions.meaning: a boy soprano's chance to sing the high part
a football pools bet that people place

explanation.walkthrough: The TREBLE CHANCE is a British football pools bet on drawn matches.
explanation.definitionFit: A boy soprano auditioning has a shot at singing the high part, and this is also a British pools wager.

clue.text: Friend at court ?

parts.note: barristers in a British court refer to one another as 'my ... friend'

explanation.surface: Someone asks who a friend in court is.
explanation.walkthrough: The courtroom formula is 'my learned friend'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawyers call each other 'my learned friend' in British courts, so the friend is erudite.

clue.text: Expiring frog ?

parts.note: to croak is both to die and to make a frog's call

explanation.surface: A frog is on its last legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Croaking is slang for dying and also the sound a frog makes.

clue.text: Intriguers make a Liberal go into transports

indicators.note: the pieces go into the middle of the word for transports

parts.note: cabs are vehicles that transport people

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician is told to take taxis.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabal is a secret political faction of plotters.

clue.text: By his — hat and staff, And his sandal shoon (Hamlet)

definitions.text: By his — hat and staff, And his sandal shoon (Hamlet)

parts.words: By his — hat and staff, And his sandal shoon (Hamlet)
parts.note: Ophelia's song describes a pilgrim by his shell-decorated hat, staff and sandals

explanation.surface: A line from Ophelia's song in Hamlet with one word blank.
explanation.walkthrough: Pilgrims wore a scallop or cockle shell on the hat as a badge.
explanation.definitionFit: A shellfish emblem on the hat marked a pilgrim, giving 'cockle hat' in Shakespeare.

clue.text: Calumets don't seem quite right with this wine

indicators.note: the letters of Calumets look wrong as they stand and must be put right

explanation.surface: Peace pipes look out of place beside a glass of sweet wine.
explanation.walkthrough: A calumet is a Native American ceremonial pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet fortified wine made from the muscat grape is this wine.

clue.text: Shoot at nought in undergrowth ?

parts.note: to pot is to shoot game
nought is the figure O

explanation.surface: Someone fires at nothing in the bushes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Undergrowth' is not shrubs but something that grows underground, the tuber.
explanation.definitionFit: The tuber develops below the soil, so it is literally growth under the ground.

clue.text: Goodbye and thanks

parts.note: British slang 'ta' means thanks, so two of them, and the doubled word is a childish farewell

explanation.surface: Someone says farewell and expresses gratitude.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is British slang for thank you.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a casual British farewell, and also 'ta' twice, informal thanks.

clue.text: Like a Horatian homestead

parts.note: the Roman poet Horace was given a farm in the hills north-east of Rome

explanation.surface: Something resembles the country house of the poet Horace.
explanation.definitionFit: Horace's famous country farm lay in the territory of an ancient Italian people, and is known by their name.

clue.text: Ref addresses a player, hounding him rather

definitions.text: Ref addresses a player, hounding him rather

parts.words: Ref addresses a player, hounding him rather
parts.note: 'Ref' is refer; a shout of 'listen' to a full-back; and the huntsman's call sending hounds back on the scent

explanation.surface: A referee speaks to a player in a badgering way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ref' is short for refer, not referee: to refer to the past. In hunting the phrase calls the hounds to retrace their path.
explanation.definitionFit: To return to an earlier subject is to refer back, and the hunting call turns hounds round.

clue.text: Urgently requests direction in an afterthought

indicators.note: the word for direction sits in the middle of the afterthought's letters

parts.note: PS, postscript, is an afterthought at the end of a letter
a lead is direction or guidance

explanation.surface: A letter's postscript asks for guidance urgently.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who begs earnestly is making urgent requests.

clue.text: Pull over without a break from here to the mainland ?

definitions.text: Pull over without a break from here to the mainland ?

parts.words: Pull over without a break from here to the mainland ?
parts.note: a knitted jumper with a traditional pattern named after a remote Shetland island, far from the Scottish mainland

explanation.surface: A driver is told to stop the car only on reaching the mainland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pull over' is a pullover, a jumper (British for sweater); the island lies between Orkney and Shetland.
explanation.definitionFit: A patterned knitted jumper is named after the small Scottish island where the style began.
